mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive >50% when FEDFUNDS is high, or Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur >60% when UNRATE rises above 3.5%, or Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rises and employment growth slows, the economy is weakening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur >60% with both signals, or Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, slowing industrial production (INDPRO) signals a downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur >50% in late-cycle, or Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur >40% with rising RSAFS, or Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur >40% when INDPRO >102, or Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL) with high FEDFUNDS indicates tight policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur >50% with both high CPI and FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansions, rising housing starts (HOUST) signal growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur >40% in early-cycle, or Rank IC <0.03.
